I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 30 years. My son works in the city now, so it's mostly me. I know what works here — I've seen the dry years and the wet ones.

My 24 mu breaks down simply: 18 mu I rotate between wheat and maize — plant wheat in October, cut it in June, put maize right back in the same ground. The other 6 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton's hard work but the price has been decent and I know how to grow it.

For the wheat, I'll do rotary tillage right after I harvest the maize in late September. I use the improved variety the seed station recommends — not the fancy expensive hybrid, but the improved line that does well in this county. Three irrigations: one before planting to get good germination moisture, one at jointing, one at heading. I'll put down nitrogen twice — base fertilizer at planting, then top dress at jointing. Two pesticide passes: herbicide in early winter, then I watch for aphids and powdery mildew in April.

For maize, I go straight in after wheat with no tillage — saves moisture, saves time. I've used Zhengdan 958 hybrid for years. It's reliable. Summer rain usually covers most of the water needs but I'll irrigate twice if we get a dry August like last year. Heavy on nitrogen — maize eats it.

For the cotton, I plough deep in spring. Bt hybrid seed so I don't fight bollworms as hard as my father did. But I still spray six times — aphids, spider mites, other insects. Five irrigations because cotton needs steady moisture especially at boll set. Cotton is what worries me most with my son gone — it takes hands.
